newsitem.title: UK: Heavy rains hampers East European sugar beet crop.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rains hampers East European sugar beet crop.

text.p: Wet weather remains the focus of interest for eastern Europe's 1996-97 beet crop and sugar production is expected to be lower than last year despite some patchy recovery, industry sources said on Tuesday.
In its first estimate of world 1996-97 sugar production, statistician F.O. Licht said east European output should fall to 9.29 million tonnes after the 9.71 million notched up last year.
Output was expected to fall sharply in both Ukraine and Russia, the region's two largest producers, although the Czech Republic and Poland were both expecting higher outputs, it said.
In Ukraine, the largest producer, farmers are seeing long harvest delays and only 10 percent of beets have been lifted.
A severe fuel shortage has been blamed for much of the delay and equipment breakdowns are also complicating the harvest, resulting in only 14,000 of 18,000 combines in working order.
The Ukrainian government has forecast a poor beet harvest of 26 million tonnes, down from last year's 30 million.
Russia still looks to be on course for a lower sugar output this year despite a slight improvement in weather conditions.
Final white sugar production is expected at less than 1.6 million tonnes from this year's crop, or less than one-third of the amount needed to meet annual demand.
Last week Viktor Sukhachyov, deputy head of the Rossakhsvyokla beet producers association said the harvest would amount to 16 million tonnes, after 19.1 million last year.

"If conditions are not favourable -- rain and frost -- then even that level may not be reached," he said. "There has been rain in many areas, but most importantly, our equipment is getting worse and worse."
Poland should turn out more sugar this year but rainy September weather may keep sugar content down. Wet weather had also been a problem for Czech beet farmers.
